# The lanes CI runs

Every workflow under `.github/workflows/` is rendered from `ci/lanes.toml` by
`ci/scripts/lanes.py`. A lane is a command with four typed properties: the host
it runs on, what it needs of that host, when it runs, and what it produces or
consumes. Everything a job spells -- its runner, container, services, edges,
condition, permissions, checkout, toolchain, artifact transfer, release gate
and summary -- is derived from those. The guard `lanes rendered` holds the
committed files equal to the table.

Locally, `python3 ci/scripts/lanes.py run <lane>` runs a lane's commands in
order inside the CI image (`ci/dev.sh python3 ci/scripts/lanes.py run <lane>`;
`--with pg,s3` provides the backends a lane needs).

## `ci.yml` -- CI

The merge gate and the release candidate: every pull request, and every push
to main. Does the tree pass its lints, its hermetic suite, its backend arms
and its guards; does every artifact a release promotes build, and run as a
user runs it. A pull request's run measures the tree; main's run compiles
what writes the shared cache (setup-rust-ci writes only on main), builds the
artifacts a release promotes, and measures what only main measures: the live
hub tests and the performance gate. Branch protection requires `ci-summary`
and an up-to-date branch, so the tree main holds is the tree a run proved.

The tree's CI images are built here when the registry lacks them (the
`CI image (...)` jobs); every other workflow waits for them.

Fires on: pr, main.

of the run that proved main's tree (a runtime base image's update, a service
patch release), the distributed lanes over main again, and the cookbook as a
reader installs it from PyPI.

## `gpu-prove.yml` -- GPU prove (RunPod)

The gated GPU suites on real NVIDIA hardware, one rented pod per shipped CUDA
arch (`crates/jammi-kernels/build.rs` GENCODE_ARCHES): the served GPU proof
and the engine-core correctness suite, built at the image's baked compute
capability and run on the device. Every release gates on this lane's recorded
verdict for the tree it promotes (`verdict.py require`), never on a fresh
rental: prove, then tag. A dispatch on a tag ref gets the release budget --
three attempts on a capacity exit and the matching timeout. Never cancelled:
a cancel SIGKILLs the runner before the driver's EXIT trap returns the pod.

Fires on: label:run-gpu, dispatch, schedule (`47 3 * * *`).

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu-prove-subject` | ubuntu | - | label:run-gpu, dispatch, schedule | - | - | Records the tree this run proves; every leg checks out that same commit, so the subject names the tree the pod built. |
| `gpu-prove` | ubuntu x4 | runpod | label:run-gpu, dispatch, schedule | - | - | One rented device per shipped CUDA arch runs the gated GPU suites at the image's baked compute capability; a dispatch on a tag ref gets three attempts on a capacity exit. |

## `gpu-howwell.yml` -- GPU how-well (RunPod)

The fine-tune how-well A/B on a rented A100: `ci/scripts/perf/finetune_run_ab.sh`
driving `jammi-bench finetune-run` per (rung, seed, take) against the
committed held-out fixture, judged by `jammi-bench ladder train-run`. Every
input is a choice an operator makes per run; the committed artifacts are what
the merge path validates (`check_cuda_run_artifacts.py`).

Fires on: dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu-howwell` | ubuntu | runpod | dispatch | - | - | The how-well A/B on a rented A100, every input an operator's choice; its evidence is uploaded for the committed artifacts a merge-path guard validates. |

## `gpu-perf-ab.yml` -- GPU perf A/B (RunPod)

The `encode` ladder's revision edge on a rented A100: `ci/scripts/perf/gpu_inference_ab.sh`
builds this checkout's merge-base with main twice (base, and rebuilt as the
A/A null) and this checkout once, runs `jammi-bench encode-step --cuda 0` on
each, and the ladder judges the revised cost against the wider of the rung's
noise band and the A/A band. The verdict is uploaded for a human; nothing
gates on it.

Fires on: label:run-gpu-perf-ab, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu-perf-ab` | ubuntu | runpod | label:run-gpu-perf-ab, dispatch | - | - | The encode revision edge on a rented A100: the verdict is uploaded for a human, and the driver's own exit codes are named. |

## `gpu-topology.yml` -- GPU topology (RunPod)

The fine-tune gang on real GPUs at every topology the engine lays a job out
as -- one host with one GPU, one host with two (in one process, and as two
processes), two hosts with two each -- under the inline and NCCL transports,
through the product path. Driven by `ci/scripts/runpod_gpu_topology.sh`.

COST BOUND (human-approved), from the driver's own defaults
(`ci/scripts/test_gpu_topology_lane.sh` re-derives them and fails when this
header and the mechanism disagree): 2 hosts x 2 GPUs x TOPOLOGY_MAX_GPU_RATE
($4.00/GPU/h, refused above it before any create) x RP_TTL_HOURS (4 h, baked
into each pod's own entrypoint):
  (i) terminate-succeeds: 4 x $4.00 x 4 h = $64.00 per run (ceiling).
  (ii) sweep-only (every terminate fails): each pod bills to its TTL, then
       gpu-reap.yml's 6-hourly sweep: 4 x $4.00 x (4 + 6) h = $160.00.

Nothing gates on this lane: it produces `topology.json`, which a human
reviews and commits under `crates/jammi-kernels/artifacts/cuda-runs/`.

Fires on: label:run-topology, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu-topology` | ubuntu | runpod | label:run-topology, dispatch | - | - | The fine-tune gang at every topology on a rented two-host fleet; one attempt per run, because a retry is a second rental search and a cost decision for a human. |

## `gpu-reap.yml` -- GPU reap (RunPod orphans)

Terminates RunPod pods this repository rented that have outlived their own
deadline: the backstop for a deadline that never got armed (a container that
died early, a host that stopped reporting). It fails when it cannot enumerate
the account's pods: "could not check" is never "nothing to clean".

Fires on: schedule, dispatch (`23 */6 * * *`).

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu-reap` | ubuntu | runpod | schedule, dispatch | - | - | Terminates the pods this repository rented that outlived their own deadline; two sweeps never overlap. |

## `cookbook-gpu.yml` -- Cookbook on a GPU

Every recipe and every page of the book, run with the real Hub models they
teach with, over the builds of the ci.yml run that proved the tree: the CUDA
engine wheel, the client wheel, the CUDA server and the CLI, installed on a
rented L4 (the class of GPU a Colab reader gets). The run records each page's
execution and assembles the book a release publishes. Every release gates on
this lane's recorded verdict for the tree it promotes: dispatch it before
tagging.

Fires on: label:cookbook-gpu, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cookbook-subject` | ubuntu | - | label:cookbook-gpu, dispatch | - | - | Records the tree this run renders the book over; the pod checks out that same commit. |
| `cookbook` | cpu-image | runpod | label:cookbook-gpu, dispatch | `cookbook-book` | `native-cu12-wheel`, `client-wheel`, `server-cu12-x86_64-binary`, `jammi-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | Every recipe and page on real Hub models over the proving run's builds, on a rented L4; the whole-book assembly then reads each page's record and executes nothing. |

## `crates.yml` -- Crates

Publishes the workspace crates to crates.io on a `v*` tag, behind the release
gate. `ci/scripts/publish_crates.sh` is the publish program: topological
order, the per-crate already-published guard, the sparse-index wait. A
dispatch on the tag finishes an interrupted release; crates.io's trusted
publisher is registered to this file.

Fires on: tag:v, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `publish-crates` | cpu-image | oidc | tag:v | - | - | Publishes the crates in topological order with a token minted and revoked around the publish; `cargo publish` verifies each crate builds, in the tree's own image. |

Publishes `@f-inverse/jammi-client` to npm on the `v*` tag that publishes the
crates, behind the release gate, through npm's OIDC trusted publishing
(registered to this file). It builds nothing: the tarball is the one the run
that proved the tag's tree packed.

Fires on: tag:v, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `publish-npm` | ubuntu | oidc, node | tag:v | - | `ts-client-package` | Publishes the packed tarball through npm's OIDC trusted publishing with provenance; a version already on npm is skipped, so a re-run is idempotent. |

## `pypi.yml` -- PyPI

Publishes every Python dist to PyPI on a `py-v*` tag, in lockstep at the
workspace version: the client `jammi-ai`, the embedded engine `jammi-ai-native`
per platform and `jammi-ai-native-cu12`, and the servers `jammi-server` per
arch and `jammi-server-cu12`. It compiles nothing: every wheel is the one the
run that proved the tag's tree built and held to PyPI's per-file limit. One
leg per PyPI project, each project's trusted publisher registered to this
file and the `pypi` environment. A dispatch on the tag finishes an
interrupted release (PyPI refuses a re-upload, so a re-run is idempotent).

Fires on: tag:py-v, dispatch.

| lane | runs on | needs | when | produces | consumes | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `publish-pypi` | ubuntu x5 | oidc | tag:py-v | - | `client-wheel`, `wheels-native-linux-x86_64`, `wheels-native-linux-aarch64`, `wheels-native-macos-arm64`, `wheels-native-macos-x86_64`, `native-cu12-wheel`, `server-cpu-x86_64-wheel`, `server-cpu-aarch64-wheel`, `server-cu12-x86_64-wheel` | One leg per PyPI project uploads every wheel of that project together: a release with one platform missing is worse than a failed release. |

## `release.yml` -- Release

The GitHub release of a `v*` tag, behind the release gate: the prebuilt
binaries attached with a provenance attestation over the exact bytes, and the
`jammi-server` container images pushed to GHCR -- the CPU image's `generic`
and `selfcontained` variants, one native leg per arch merged into the real
tags by the one verify-then-promote definition (`merge-index`), and the CUDA
image -- every pushed digest attested and verified. One tag policy
(`ci/scripts/image_tags.sh`): `:X.Y.Z`, `:X.Y`, `:sha-<sha>`, `:latest`.
Every image packages binaries the proving run built and compiles nothing.

Fires on: tag:v, dispatch.

| `server-image-cpu` | ubuntu x4 | ghcr, attest | tag:v | - | `server-cpu-{target}-binary`, `jammi-{triple}` | The CPU image's variant x arch legs, each packaging the proving run's binaries and pushing only its own immutable commit tag, attested and verified. |
| `server-image-cpu-merge` | ubuntu x2 | ghcr, attest | tag:v | - | - | Merges each CPU variant's per-arch legs into the real tags through the one verify-then-promote definition, and attests the merged digest. |
